rows.rationale: No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over an architectural BRIEF vocabulary in the first place: the 266 kinds are mechanically derived from this subset's own 66 registers by `📓️derivation-rules.md` — every header-shaped id-keyed register yields create/delete/rename/replace (rule 2), the two edge-shaped registers (`adjacencies`, `traces`) yield connect/disconnect instead (rule 4), and the three document-level scalar facets (`meta`, `project`, `governance`) yield rename/replace (rule 1). That derivation is a specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute. What stands in its place is the committed, independently handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` specification vector under each of the 266 `🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` leaves — 260 of which move the document — plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: applying a kind and then its OWN computed inverse must restore the exact pre-mutation vector.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Block5dMutation` — the widest vocabulary in this plugin, defining a part kind that carries BOTH a 2d and a 3d facet at once, a representation catalogue with LODs and tags, grip kinds and placed grips in two dimensionalities (`move-grip2d`, `move-grip3d`, `resize-grip3d`), and two independent editor cameras. Its diff also renames the two facet fields — the snapshot calls them `2d` and `3d`, names no Rust identifier can carry, and the diff calls them `part2d`/`part3d`. That mapping IS this subset's specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability and footprint completeness, the latter resolving `2d`/`3d` through the declared alias table before it decides anything.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Block3dMutation` — the definition of an object kind whose vortex-kind vocabulary is SPLIT across two places: a shared catalogue held as a child document reference in `catalog`, and this document's own additions in `vortexKindExtra`. `create-vortex-kind` and `delete-vortex-kind` move BOTH at once and the diff declares them through a single `vortexKinds` field, so a reader that assumed a diff field mirrors a snapshot field would mis-measure every one of those kinds. That split IS this subset's specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability and footprint completeness, the latter resolving both `catalog` and `vortexKindExtra` through the declared alias table.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Puzzle3dMutation` — the widest vocabulary in this plugin, spanning FOUR independent top-level collections (`objects`, `attractions`, `targetVolumes`, `references`) where an attraction names its endpoints as `object:vortex` pairs and a vortex lives inside an object, so `connect-vortices` and `disconnect-vortices` join two collections that have no containment relationship at all. That is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external 3d-scene library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection, or, where the committed outcome itself declares `mutation.no-op`, must provably move nothing) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares).

No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and no photogrammetry library is authoritative over `RemodelMutation` — this is a reconstruction JOB document, not a point cloud or a mesh file, so a reader of COLMAP, LAS or PLY output would be judging a different artifact. What distinguishes this subset is that its 35 kinds fall into three genuinely different families with different laws: id-keyed create/delete/change over five referential pools (`streams`, `assets`, camera calibrations, rig extrinsics, GCPs — where deleting a stream or a GCP CASCADES into observations that point at it), `update-*-params` over the eight inseparable `ReconstructionParams` sub-records (each replaced whole because its fields are only meaningful together), and `replace-*` over the engine-owned result payloads. Confidence comes from the committed per-kind specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, already unit-tested inside the production crate, plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property — which for the cascading deletes means the undone document must carry the cascaded observations back, not merely the deleted record. `commit-reconstruction` is the one kind with NO committed vector: its diff reads process-global staging state (`commit_staged_remodel_reconstruction`, `durable_staged_remodel_asset`) that a `(before, mutation, after)` triple cannot carry, so `mutate-remodel-1` exercises it through its own documented refusal path instead and says so in its feature description.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none could be authoritative over `NoteMutation` in any case: the 33 kinds ARE this subset's specification — 9 document-root scalars (the title plus the eight grid/snap/tool settings), 3 id-keyed image-asset kinds, and 21 kinds over an id-keyed, z-ordered, group-NESTABLE block tree whose leaves carry four different typed contents (text, math, ink strokes and tables). No external reader has a model of that tree to check ours against. What stands in its place is the committed, independently handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` specification vector under each of the 33 `🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` leaves — every one of which moves the document, which is not true of any other artifact covered in this wave — plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: applying a kind and then its OWN computed inverse must restore the exact pre-mutation vector, POSITION in the block tree included and not merely membership.

`s.shooting.shooting` is a semio-NATIVE artifact. Its persisted document is the `shooting.shooting.dsl` envelope — `semio shooting.shooting.dsl v1` followed by a handcrafted block/table grammar with typed columns (`[id:TEXT name:TEXT url:TEXT format:TEXT origin:CRD orientation:TUPLE scale:TUPLE]`) and `deg`-suffixed angle literals — and no package in any ecosystem reads or writes it, because that grammar is defined by this repository alone. There is therefore nothing to register, and no library is authoritative over `ShootingMutation`: that vocabulary IS this subset's own specification. The nearest candidates were surveyed and DECLINED rather than merely absent, and unlike the sibling semio-native vocabularies this one has real domain competitors, so the decision has to be argued. (1) The 3D-scene interchange formats — glTF 2.0 (`gltf`), USD, Collada — do carry an asset list, a transform per asset, a camera list and a punctual-light block, so a naive reading suggests a differential is possible. It is not, and the reason is structural rather than cosmetic: this document's `shots` collection has no counterpart in any of them. A shot is a RENDER REQUEST — width, height, output format, mask shape, background, and a reference to a saved camera — and eleven of the thirty-one kinds address it. A glTF reader asked to judge `change-shot-format` or `change-shot-shape` would have nothing to read, so eleven kinds would silently report agreement about a field the reference does not model. That is precisely the shape of green this wave exists to stop. (2) A generic JSON or YAML reader is rejected for the same reason as every other subset here: it supplies a DOM and no knowledge of an id-keyed collection, a quaternion orientation or a scene lighting block, so all thirty-one semantics would still be hand-written on top of it. Confidence comes instead from specification vectors of unusual strength: this subset's thirty-one committed per-kind leaf fixtures under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/` share ONE byte-identical committed before-snapshot (SHA-1 `6441b72754e5c649b2b07a2f2b244313467f85a0`, verified across all thirty-one), so the vocabulary comes with a complete, independently authored `(before, mutation, after)` suite already — and from the metamorphic laws the case asserts in role: every kind must MOVE the semantic projection, every kind's own computed inverse must restore it exactly, and the committed real DSL artifact must survive decode/encode byte-for-byte.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Puzzle5dMutation` — a vocabulary in which ONE part carries BOTH a 2d and a 3d facet, so `move-part2d` and `move-part3d` are different kinds addressing different halves of the same record, and in which `kindCompatibility` is a TOP-LEVEL field rather than a member of `meta` as it is in the sibling 2d and 3d subsets. That is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection, or, where the committed outcome itself declares `mutation.no-op`, must provably move nothing) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares).

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Puzzle2dMutation` — a vocabulary in which handles live INSIDE nodes while the edges that join them are a sibling top-level collection, so `add-node-handle`, `connect-handles` and `disconnect-handles` reach across two collections at once, and in which the kind catalogs and the compatibility relation live in `meta` rather than beside the elements they govern. That is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external diagram or graph library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection, or, where the committed outcome itself declares `mutation.no-op`, must provably move nothing) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares).

No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `LayoutMutation`. What distinguishes this subset from every sibling is that a layout document is FOUR pools at two nesting depths joined by reference: document-root scalars (`name`, `printTarget`, `dataFieldsJson`), the id-keyed root collections `pages`, `stories` and `links`, and — nested one level down, inside a page — that page's own `layers` and `frames`. A frame is therefore addressed by (page, frame) rather than by id alone, a text frame names its `stories` member by id and an image frame names its `links` member by id, so `delete-story` and `delete-link` reach ACROSS pools into frames that point at them, while `reorder-pages` moves a whole nested subtree. Confidence comes from the committed per-kind specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — a `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: applying a kind and then its own computed inverse must restore the exact pre-mutation document, including a deleted page's ORIGINAL index and its whole frame subtree, which a deletion undone by re-appending would not. The `mutate-layout-1` case re-exercises those SAME committed bytes end-to-end through `apply_layout_mutation`/`inverse_layout_mutation`.

`s.stdio.semio` is the ENVELOPE union over all eighteen semio subsets; there is no third-party crate that reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, and there could not be one authoritative over a vocabulary whose eighteen wrapper variants each embed another semio-native subset's own mutation enum. What this subset OWNS is not the payload semantics — those belong to the eighteen arms and are covered by their own leaf fixtures and their own cases — but the envelope-level ROUTING: does a wrapped mutation whose arm matches the base snapshot's arm thread through, does a MISMATCHED one get refused with `mutation.target-missing` instead of silently corrupting the document, and is `set-snapshot` genuinely the only verb that can change the subset kind. Every scenario is written against exactly that, with a projection the envelope can answer without naming any arm's snapshot type: `{schema, subset, diagnostics, matchesReference}`. Confidence comes from the committed `(before, mutation, after, diff)` specification vector under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📄set-snapshot/🧪️tests/`, already unit-tested inside the production crate, plus the routing and inverse laws as metamorphic properties. Honest limits, recorded rather than papered over: the eighteen delegating arms are exercised against each arm's OWN empty snapshot rather than a real-world document, because no real-world `.semio` artifact exists outside this repository and the committed example assets can only be decoded through `store::ArtifactDsl`/`store::ArtifactPack`, traits reached solely via a private extern-crate alias that nothing re-exports — the same structural gap wave 7 recorded for `kit`, `object`, `text` and `table`. Re-exporting those two traits would let this case read the committed `.dsl.semio` examples directly and is the single change that would most strengthen it. WAVE-14 RE-SURVEY (cross-language differential oracles, ticket 26/08/23): a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language was built for five sibling subsets in this same artifact and works end to end, so the route was re-examined here and REJECTED on two concrete, nameable blockers rather than on absence. First, the envelope's own committed documents declare the wrapped arm OPAQUE: the snapshot grammar's `document = artifact-mark subset-line REST` hands off to the arm's own grammar, the binary protocol models the wrapped pack as one opaque trailing `payload` chain, and the mutations grammar is `op = "noMutation" | tag ":" REST`. An envelope-level second implementation can therefore reproduce both committed carriers byte for byte - and it can - but it can say nothing about whether a DELEGATED verb changed the arm it reached, which is exactly what eighteen of this vocabulary's twenty kinds measure. Answering that honestly needs a second implementation of eighteen separate subset vocabularies, not of this one. Second, nothing lets the two languages read the same arm input: this subset exports `parse_semio_envelope_dsl`/`print_semio_envelope_dsl` and `decode_semio_envelope_pack`/`encode_semio_envelope_pack` but NO JSON bridge for `SemioSnapshot` or `SemioMutation`, so the arm snapshots and the wrapped verbs can only be constructed in Rust, inside the subject crate, where a second language cannot see them. Registering a Python oracle that merely restated the routing table would be a transcribed expectation wearing an oracle's name - our own answer on both sides - and is the one thing this platform exists to prevent, so it was not done. The two changes that would unblock a real differential here, in order of leverage: export a JSON bridge for `SemioSnapshot`/`SemioMutation` the way `✳️cad` and `✳️document` already do, and re-export `store::ArtifactDsl`/`store::ArtifactPack` so an external adapter can decode the committed example assets. A third, smaller finding recorded here rather than filed away: the committed snapshot grammar's `subset-tag` production still lists only thirteen tags (brep, mesh, model, value, document, cad, drawing, image, video, audio, animation, presentation, flow) while this catalog and the sibling mutations grammar both declare eighteen arms - `text`, `table`, `graph`, `object` and `kit` are missing from it.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `CadMutation` — a vocabulary of CHILD-SLOT LIFECYCLE (the four fixed `shapeModel`/`buildingModel`/`energyModel`/`structureClassicModel` slots plus the `drawings` collection), a node tree, and per-model-definition reference lists. That vocabulary IS this subset's specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute; registering a general-purpose CAD or JSON-patch crate to judge it would put a library that has never seen this document model in the position of the reference, which is worse than recording no oracle at all. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares, which is the precondition that makes the mutation undoable at all).

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `LowpolyMutation` — a vocabulary over a document with exactly TWO top-level fields, `schema` and an id-keyed `objects` list whose members each carry an INDEX-keyed, anonymous `paintLayers` sub-collection. That two-level addressing is the whole point of the vocabulary and it is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external mesh or scene library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares, which is the precondition that makes the mutation undoable at all).

`process.process3d` is a semio-NATIVE artifact — a fabrication document holding a workshop of machines, a stock body and an ordered timeline of process steps, all in `.dsl.semio` — and nothing outside this repository reads it. Two candidate families were surveyed and DECLINED. G-code parsers (`gcode`, `nom-gcode`) model a flat instruction stream with no machine catalogue, no capability recipes and no undoable edit vocabulary, so they could adjudicate none of these sixteen kinds; and STEP/BREP kernels (`ruststep`, already registered under `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio`'s `📐️step` subsets) model solid geometry, which is only the payload of `replace-stock-solid` and says nothing about the timeline, the workshop or the replay cursor. Evidence is the sixteen committed specification vectors plus the inverse law. That evidence is UNEVEN and the feature says so kind by kind: nine vectors are forward and observable, but the seven step-scoped verbs are implemented today as documented no-ops — their `diff` builders take `_payload`/`_base` by underscore and return `MutationOutcome::empty().warn("mutation.no-op", …)` because the timeline is a composed `s.stdio.semio.flow` child and no link resolver exists yet — so their vectors record `before == after` and their `mutate-`/`inverse-` scenarios can assert only the declared no-op, never the forward semantics.

`s.mathematical.mathematical` is a semio-NATIVE artifact. Its persisted body is three composed child handles (`notation` → `s.stdio.semio.text`, `results` → `s.stdio.semio.table`, `computed` → `s.stdio.semio.value`) plus ONE plain field, `equation`: a labelled expression AST whose `EquationNodeLabel` allocator only ever increases, so an address survives edits that a positional path would not. Both candidate families were surveyed and DECLINED. `petgraph` is the credible Rust graph library, but it models a graph as an in-memory container — it cannot read `.dsl.semio`, it has no notion of node labels, positions, an algorithm selector or a directedness flag, and it has no editing vocabulary whose results could be compared with ours. On the algebra side an external CAS is likewise the wrong instrument: `symbolica` is commercially licensed and cannot be linked here, and the small expression crates (`meval`, `evalexpr`) EVALUATE a string rather than exposing an authored, labelled AST, so none of them can adjudicate `change-coefficient`, which edits a numbered term in place. Evidence is the fifteen committed specification vectors plus the inverse law — and, recorded here rather than hidden, that evidence is thin for thirteen of the fifteen kinds: the graph and point-cloud verbs address collections that live in composed children the fixtures cannot resolve, so nine of them carry `rejected` vectors (`mutation.target-missing`, `mutation.duplicate-id`) and four carry `applied`-but-`mutation.no-op` vectors. Only `change-coefficient` and `insert-point` carry a forward, observable vector.

No third party reads or writes `.dag.dsl.semio`/`.dag.pack.semio`, and no graph library holds an opinion about the two things this vocabulary actually decides. First, `DagSnapshot` persists NO nodes and NO edges: it carries `schema` plus one composed `s.stdio.semio.graph` child handle whose `childId` is a content digest of the child, so what an applied mutation produces is a NEW handle and what a refused one produces is the same handle — an addressing scheme private to this repository. Second, the vocabulary is a DAG vocabulary, not a graph one: `connect-nodes` refuses a self-loop and refuses any edge whose target can already reach its source (`🔗connect-nodes/🔺️diff/🦀️component.rs::would_create_cycle`), and endpoints are `node@port` strings split by this plugin's own `split_endpoint`. A general graph crate asked to adjudicate either would be answering a different question. Confidence comes instead from the fourteen committed, independently handcrafted specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one per kind, each already unit-tested inside the production crate itself — and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property. Those fourteen vectors are ALL rejection vectors, and deliberately so: the leaf tests state the reason in as many words (`🌱create-node/🧪️tests/rejects-a-duplicate-node-id/🦀️component.rs`) — hand-authoring an APPLIED `➡️after` would mean hand-forging a `std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher` digest, a value the standard library explicitly does not specify. `mutate-dag-1` therefore runs each vector for its exact `(code, severity, target)` triple AND separately applies a real-effect payload of its own to the committed five-node example document, where the content-addressed handle supplies the observability the vectors cannot.

No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `DrawMutation`. The vocabulary is not a generic tree-edit list either: it is derived from `DrawSnapshot`'s RECURSIVE layer tree, where a layer is one of several node kinds (group, path, trace, …) sharing a `base` record, so `update-layer-trace-params` exists only for the trace node kind while `set-layer-boolean-operation`, `replace-layer-fill` and `replace-layer-stroke` reach into the shared `attributes` record, and `create-layer`/`duplicate-layer`/`reorder-layer` address a PARENT plus an index rather than a flat position. Layer ids are content-addressed, which is why `create-layer` with an existing node is a hard rejection rather than a duplicate. Confidence comes from the committed per-kind specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — a `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: applying a kind and then its own computed inverse must restore the exact pre-mutation document, POSITION in the tree included. The `mutate-draw-1` case re-exercises those SAME committed bytes end-to-end through `apply_draw_mutation`/`inverse_draw_mutation`, and crosses the real committed `Semio Emblem` drawing through both of its codecs for the identity law.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Procedural2dMutation` — a vocabulary that differs from its 3d sibling exactly where the two documents' editing models differ: whole-value `replace-widget`/`replace-synapse` instead of field-wise `update-*`, and a document-wide `clear-widget-layout` instead of a per-widget `delete-widget-position`. Which of those two shapes is correct for this subset IS the specification, not a fact an external node-graph library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares).

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `Procedural3dMutation` — a vocabulary over a document that is a COMPOSITION of two unrelated halves, a `fixture` (widget/synapse graph plus camera and layout) and a `generation` (a parameter-set history with a selection), so every one of its fourteen kinds lands in one of exactly TWO top-level fields. That is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external node-graph library could confirm or refute. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one handcrafted `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — replayed end-to-end through the test platform here, plus two metamorphic laws asserted in role: observability (a kind must move the compared projection) and footprint completeness (`before` and `after` may differ on exactly the fields the committed diff declares).

There is no credible third-party crate that is authoritative over plain-text line structure: line splitting on LF/CRLF, uniform-per-document line-ending policy and trailing-newline presence are exactly what THIS subset defines, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute independently. The closest candidate, the `csv` crate already linked for the tabular subsets, genuinely helps for a NARROW part of this: with quoting disabled and a delimiter byte that cannot appear in real text, its record reader independently confirms this subset's own line-boundary splitting on single-style (no mixed CR/LF/CRLF), NON-BLANK real content — but a standalone probe found `csv-core`'s NFA silently treats a zero-byte record as "not a record" and never emits it (confirmed unconditionally, not a `Terminator`-mode artifact), so it cannot cross-check the true line count on any real prose that has blank lines at all, which most real text does (the real fixture below has 80, measured). It cannot discharge a full differential comparison either way: it collapses LF/CR/CRLF into one undifferentiated boundary and never reports which terminator it saw, so it cannot confirm or refute this subset's central claim (LF vs CRLF vs trailing-newline presence). Confidence instead comes from specification vectors (CRLF/LF/mixed, no trailing terminator, a BOM, astral-plane characters, combining marks, and NEL/LS/PS explicitly NOT treated as separators — all carried directly in the feature file as literal byte-exact local:// fixtures) and the inverse law as a metamorphic property (apply a mutation, apply its computed inverse, the real document's projection must return to the original) plus an independently hand-written reference implementation of the mutation semantics in this subset's own oracle module, which never calls this subset's production `TxtSnapshot`/`TxtMutation` code.

`s.flow.flow` is a semio-NATIVE artifact. Its persisted document is the `flow.flow` envelope (`semio flow.flow.dsl v1` followed by a JSON body) and its widget graph lives in a composed `s.stdio.semio.flow` CHILD addressed by a content-derived handle. No package in any ecosystem reads or writes that envelope — the preamble and the child-handle addressing are defined by this repository alone — so there is nothing to register, and no library is authoritative over `FlowMutation`: that vocabulary IS this subset's own specification. The nearest candidates were surveyed and DECLINED rather than merely absent, and the first one is unusually close, which is why the decision has to be argued rather than assumed. (1) This document's BODY is plain JSON and json-rust 0.12 is already linked into the stdio oracle crate, so a json-rust-mediated differential is technically reachable. It would still be a weak oracle of exactly the kind the wave brief forbids: json-rust supplies a generic DOM and no knowledge of a widget discriminant, a synapse port pair, a layout entry or the cascade `delete-widget` performs on the synapses that touched the deleted widget, so all ten mutation semantics — the entire content of this catalog — would still be hand-written on top of it, and calling that hand-written code a third-party reference would overstate the evidence rather than add any. A generic container parser is not a reference implementation of the vocabulary carried inside the container. (2) The node-graph domain has real third-party readers (Graphviz DOT, GraphML, and the node-graph formats of several DCC tools), and they were rejected on a substantive point: none carries a typed widget UNION whose variant decides its own field set, and none carries `duplicate-widget`, a COMPOSITE that plans a widget insert and a synapse insert together and therefore has no framework-generic counterpart at all (see `to_framework_mutation`'s own doc comment). A differential against one would compare two different documents. Two independent reasons, and the first is the decisive one. (1) NO CANDIDATE CAN SEE THE AXES. This vocabulary addresses the SOF marker byte, the frame's sample precision, whether a DAC arithmetic-conditioning segment is present, the per-class Huffman table count and each component's sampling factors — every one of them a field of the frame header or the entropy-coding mode. `image` 0.25 is registered by the sibling ✳️any subset and is the right reference for a JPEG raster, but its public API hands back pixels, dimensions and a colour type; it exposes no frame header, no SOFn discriminant, no DAC flag and no DHT view, and it offers no way to WRITE any of them either. `jpeg-decoder` exposes only an `ImageInfo`. A reference that cannot express the mutation cannot adjudicate it, and registering one anyway to satisfy the workflow would be selecting a weak oracle mechanically. (2) EVEN A PERFECT ORACLE WOULD BE MEASURING NOTHING AT THE BYTE LEVEL, because this repository's own `encode_jpg` writes a conforming baseline file and no other kind of JPEG at all: it emits `FF C0` for the frame marker, precision 8, a fixed three-component 4:2:0 sampling array, exactly four DHT segments and never a DAC — so every axis this vocabulary moves is normalized away on re-serialization. That is a real, documented property of the codec (stated in the vocabulary's own module docstring), not a gap. The substitutes are therefore the standard's own tables — ITU-T T.81 Table B.1 for the SOFn marker codes, §4.2 for the 8-bit precision mandate, Annex F for Huffman-only entropy coding, §B.2.4.2 for the four-table-per-class ceiling and §B.2.2 for the 1..=4 sampling factors — read against `check_baseline_conformance`, which is where the class verdict actually lives; plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property over the decoded snapshot. `mutate-jpg-jfif-1-01-baseline` measures the vocabulary there and says in as many words that it makes no byte-level claim, except in `identity-round-trip`, which does re-encode and reads both sides through the INDEPENDENT `image` reader the ✳️any subset registers.

A raw byte buffer carries no format — it is bytes, full stop. There is no grammar for a third-party library to parse, no independent reader to project both sides through, and no credible reference WRITER either: agreeing or disagreeing with some arbitrary crate would measure that crate's own opinion of what 'a buffer' is, not a defect in this subset. The specification IS the mutation vocabulary itself (`BinaryMutation`'s five variants and their documented offset/remove_len contract in `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🦀️component.rs`), so the evidence is the specification vectors below plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property — both discharged by this module's own independently written splice/append/truncate implementation (`../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs`), which never touches the subject's `BinaryDiff`/`apply_binary_mutation`.

DWG is a proprietary, undocumented format. The only independent implementation of any weight is LibreDWG, which is GPL-3.0 C: linking it would put a copyleft C library on this repository's test host, and no owner ruling permits that. No permissively licensed Rust DWG reader exists at all — `dxf` 0.6, the crate registered for the sibling 🖊️dxf artifact, reads DXF (the PUBLISHED interchange format Autodesk documents) and explicitly not DWG. Confidence instead comes from specification vectors and the metamorphic laws, exercised against a real 148,638-byte committed architectural drawing by an independently hand-written reader/writer of the one part of DWG that IS publicly specified: the plain preamble every file since R13 begins with — six ASCII version characters at 0x00-0x05, the `maint_version` byte at 0x12, and the little-endian `codepage` u16 at 0x13-0x14, the offsets LibreDWG's own `header.spec` documents and this subset's `DwgSnapshot` doc comments already cite (and which the real fixture confirms: 0x02 and 30/ANSI_1252). That reader never calls this repository's own 12,000-line R2004+ decoder. The narrowness is real and is stated rather than hidden: everything after the preamble is the R2004+ section map — compressed, checksummed and section-encrypted — which nothing in this repository or in the permissively licensed Rust ecosystem can regenerate, so it is carried through unchanged and the projection covers the preamble triple plus the document length only. `byteLength` is what keeps `set-snapshot` (a whole-document replacement) distinguishable from `set-version-info` (a field set in place) rather than the two collapsing into one indistinguishable edit.
